To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adhesive strength of GIC for bracket bonding is significantly influenced by the structure of the tooth enamel.

GIC attaches significantly worse to the surface of impacted teeth and the teeth of adolescents than to the surface of erupted teeth in adults, which can be explained by the different surface characteristics.
GIC is a promising alternative to conventional bonding materials for bracket fixation, especially for adults.

the adhesive strength of the glass ionomer ciment is not sufficient for bracket bonding, especially in adolescents.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bonding of GIC to the enamel of the impacted teeth is not satisfactory.
GIC is a good alternative to conventional bonding materials.
the bonding of GIC to the enamel of adolescents is not as good as to adult teeth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adhesive strength of GIC is influenced by the surface properties of the enamel.
the adhesive strength of the GIC is significantly better in adult enamel than in adolescent or impacted enamel.
GIC is a suitable material for bracket fixation in adults, and that the use of this material is associated with less damage to the enamel than with other bonding materials.
